key_insight: IDiom is an autoregressive protein language model for intrinsically disordered regions, and RL-SAE lets users steer generation by rewarding sparse autoencoder features linked to desired functions.
engineering_relevance: The work provides an interpretable, composable design framework for generating IDR sequences with controllable properties, useful for synthetic biology and protein engineering workflows.
method: Train IDiom on 54M predicted IDRs curated from the AlphaFold Database.
Use sparse autoencoder features as explicit control targets during post-training reinforcement learning (RL-SAE).
Compare generated sequences against steering and supervised fine-tuning across multiple IDR design tasks.
evidence_signal: Across eight IDR design tasks, RL-SAE sequences activated about 90% of 30 targeted features on average, versus 24% for activation steering, and improved predicted subcellular localization and transcriptional activity.
watch_item: Performance depends on predicted features and disorder annotations, so transfer to experimentally validated IDR functions may require careful biological validation.
paper_title: Generative modeling of intrinsically disordered protein regions by reinforcing sparse autoencoder features
